title: Building MCP Servers in .NET
description: Develop high-performance Model Context Protocol servers in C# using stdio and ASP.NET Core SSE transports.

data.text: Architecting an MCP Server in C#

An MCP server is an executable application that responds to standardized JSON-RPC 2.0 requests from MCP clients (such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, or your custom ASP.NET Core web apps). In .NET, an MCP server can be hosted as a lightweight console application communicating over standard input/output (stdio), or as an ASP.NET Core Minimal API service exposing Server-Sent Events (SSE) for remote consumption.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: MCP servers respond to JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol methods: initialize, tools/list, and tools/call
Stdio transport uses Console standard input and output streams for zero-latency local tool calling
Always provide explicit JSON Schemas for tool inputs including required fields and property types
Return structured tool execution results using the standard content array envelope
Host in ASP.NET Core with SSE when building remote multi-tenant enterprise MCP microservices
data.takeaway: Building MCP servers in .NET allows enterprise teams to expose mission-critical databases, telemetry, and business systems to any AI client safely and efficiently.
